Q: Is there a way to tie code to multiple GAS using clasp for testing? A:

There is now a native solution for this in clasp v3: create multiple .clasp.json files and specify the one you want to target with the new --project option.

I stumbled across this in the README. It does not seem to be mentioned in Google's App Script docs, or discussed elsewhere, but works well in my experience.

For your production/dummy scenario, you might want to use .clash.json for the dummy project so a naive clasp push doesn't clobber production. You can then use, say clasp --project prod.clasp.json push for pushing to production.

My use case is actually pushing to multiple targets, and I got my threads mixed up. Below is my original answer for that use case, which provides some further guidance, albeit not directly relevant to the OP.

Clasp v2

  1. Storing multiple targets in the .clasp.json file was proposed in #349. It was closed in favour of the next option:
  2. The clasp setting command was added in #350. So now at least you can script it with something like clasp setting scriptId id1 && clasp push && clasp setting scriptId id2 && clasp push.
  3. Storing multiple targets in the .clasp.json file was again proposed in #625. It was closed in favour of the next option:
  4. Multi-developer workflow support was proposed in #991 and is still open. Personally I can't see how this would help anyway.
  5. Two entire node projects provide just this functionality. The latest is multi-clasp2.
  6. A hybrid of #1 and #2 is possible by creating multiple json files and cping them into place one at a time. Eg. (not tested) for f in *.clasp.json; do cp "$f" .clasp.json; clasp push; done
  7. As described in #350, switch to a "standalone" script instead of a "container bound" script. Container bound (attached to a particular document) scripts have more capabilities, but it turns out there are tricks to get a standalone script to act as a container bound script by specifying the scriptId.
    • This may have limitations (like complexity and speed?) that I haven't explored.

For me, #2 and #6 are pretty neck and neck. I went with #2 because it's just a single extra file, a deploy.sh. You could even replace the scriptId in the actual .clasp.json file is a dummy value, and replace it at the end of the deploy.sh, to keep the working copy clean and force the correct deploy method.

Clasp v3

Grr, all the guidance I found and documented above turns out to be associated with clasp v2. For v3, setting has gone. The best option now seems to be #6 above, which is simplified by the new --project flag.

First create multiple <id>.clasp.json files instead of the one .clasp.json file, where <id> is some unique identifier.

Then run a script like this to use each one in turn:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Call `clasp push` for each of the clasp.json files
# to automatically push to multiple Google documents.
# Ref: https://stackoverflow.com/a/79996941/3697870

set -e
shopt -s nullglob

# Execute commands from the script directory.
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

for f in *.clasp.json; do
    set -x
    clasp --project "$f" push
    { set +x; } 2>/dev/null
done

Q: Why does Selenium/Playwright keep getting detected by Cloudflare even with stealth options? A:

I don’t think you're missing a flag because everything on your list patches the JavaScript layer. It is Cloudflare/DataDome detecting you before your JS runs.

Some thoughts:

  • Headless Chromium's TLS handshake (JA3/JA4) looks automated regardless of stealth plugins. UA=real Chrome, TLS=headless. You could try curl_cffi for non-JS pages, or a patched build like Camoufox/Nodriver for rendered ones.

  • Puppeteer/Playwright drives over Chrome DevTools Protocol, and Turnstile probes for it. Stealth can't hide that the transport is CDP. I’d try a driver without CDP or headed mode with a real profile.

  • Try binding one proxy + fingerprint + cookies to a session, hold it across pages, then rotate the whole bundle.

Would look like TLS impersonation → CDP-less driver → sticky sessions.

Q: Can I defer the execution of a pipeline assignment A:

I don't think there is a clean workaround to this other than offering the consumer to decide what they want to do via switch parameter to output the IEnumerator / IEnumerable optionally when present:

function New-Range {
    param(
        [int] $Start = 0,
        [int] $Count = 10,
        [switch] $AsEnumerable)

    $ienumerable = [System.Linq.Enumerable]::Select(
        [System.Linq.Enumerable]::Range($Start, $Count),
        [System.Func[int, int]] { Start-Sleep 1; $args[0] })

    if ($AsEnumerable) { return , $ienumerable }
    $ienumerable
}

# streams output, takes 10 seconds
New-Range | ForEach-Object { "[$_]" }

# deferred execution, takes no time
$ienumerable = New-Range -AsEnumerable
# takes 10 seconds when enumerating it
$ienumerable | ForEach-Object { "[$_]" }

Q: Why do JavaScript bitwise operators return wrapped-around results for large, but still “safe” integers? A:

According to the ECMAScript specification on >>, the left operand is passed into the abstract operation ToInt32 whose description reads:

The abstract operation ToInt32 converts its argument to one of 232 integer values in the range −231 through 231−1, inclusive. This abstract operation functions as follows:

And whose behavior is specified as:

  1. Let posInt be sign(number) * floor(abs(number)).
  2. Let int32bit be posInt modulo 232; that is, a finite integer value k of Number type with positive sign and less than 232 in magnitude such that the mathematical difference of posInt and k is mathematically an integer multiple of 232.
  3. If int32bit is greater than or equal to 231, return int32bit − 232, otherwise return int32bit.

Thus, no result from >> can be greater than 231, and any value that would be greater is transformed by modulo 232 (with negative overflow for values greater than 231).

Q: Call PHP function from Twig template A:

Its not possible to access any PHP function inside Twig directly.

What you can do is write a Twig extension. A common structure is, writing a service with some utility functions, write a Twig extension as bridge to access the service from twig. The Twig extension will use the service and your controller can use the service too.

Take a look: http://symfony.com/doc/current/cookbook/templating/twig_extension.html
